question: Can the 2009 UNP Research Journal inventory support fish occurrence assertions for four named Abra and Ilocos Sur rivers, and what evidence is required before any reuse?

source.citation: Segismundo, A. B., & Felicitas, A. B. (2009). The Edible Fauna of Some Rivers in Abra and Ilocos Sur. UNP Research Journal, XVIII, 15–26.
source.licenseFinding: No item-specific open license or permission was found on the full PDF or indexed article record. A current journal submissions page describes transfer of copyright to the journal for accepted manuscripts, but its applicability to this 2009 article was not established. Public availability does not itself grant reuse rights.

methods.designAsReported: Descriptive edible-fauna inventory. One data collector was assigned per river for five days per week over eight months. Samples were reportedly preserved and brought to the National Museum Zoological Laboratory for identification and scientific-name verification.
methods.siteResolution: The paper names one river in Ilocos Sur and three in Abra but provides no coordinates, station-to-river geometry, or voucher accession numbers in the reviewed material. The printed name Burgos River is not independently resolved to a unique hydrographic feature.
methods.identificationResolution: The results describe some fish as identified and others as unidentified; the abstract reports 15 identified of 21 Baay fish, 12 of 13 Tineg fish, 13 of 14 Malanas fish, and 16 of 19 Burgos fish. The text-extracted tables contain broken or ambiguous taxon strings and do not provide museum accession crosswalks. No names were silently corrected or projected to present-day accepted taxa.
methods.scopeLimit: The article's combined edible-fauna richness counts include fish and invertebrates. They must not be interpreted as fish-only richness. The survey describes historical collection/catch in 2001; it does not establish current presence, abundance, full catchment coverage, or year-round occurrence.

reuseAndDisposition.sourceUse: Research lead only, with minimal bibliographic attribution and a bounded summary of the study's scope and limitations.
reuseAndDisposition.reason: This is valuable historical inland-water evidence, but the fieldwork is from 2001, exact sites and specimen accessions are not established, the extracted name table needs image-level transcription and taxonomic review, and no reuse license for this article was verified.

nextAction: Seek a current, reusable river survey or item-specific permission. If revisiting this paper, manually verify every proposed name from the page images, obtain a site/voucher crosswalk from the authors or National Museum, and review each taxon with a current fish-name authority before creating research-ledger assertions.

sources.supports: Full 12-page publisher-hosted article, citation, 2001 field period, named rivers, counts, methods, identification claims and tables.
Journal-volume metadata, article title, authors and abstract.
Current journal submissions page's copyright notice; it is not treated as proof of the 2009 article's specific license or retroactive terms.
